text: Any person who fails to comply with such conditions is guilty of an offence.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: I refer to Dr Chia Shi-Lu, Mr Melvin Yong and Mr Louis Ng's comments on public health research and the use and disclosure of individually-identifiable information.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: There are criteria under section 59A that the Director of Medical Services considers before conducting public health research, including whether the research can acquire new knowledge and benefit public health.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: My Ministry may not have the resources to perform complex research and may appoint institutions to conduct them and share the outcomes with us.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: Individually-identifiable information or samples will be used only if the Director of Medical Services is satisfied that the research can only be carried out with such identifiable information or samples.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: My Ministry will ensure that there are proper safeguards to protect such information or samples.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: Mr Murali Pillai asked about how the list of prescribed infectious disease under section 6 will be drawn up.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: The amendments to section 6, read together with the new provision in section 73(4)(a), allow my Ministry to distinguish between the infectious diseases that medical practitioners, laboratories or a specific class of persons, are required to notify, by prescribing the infectious diseases applicable to each group.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: For example, some diseases can only be confirmed by a laboratory test.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: Take the case of Salmonella food-borne infection causing diarrhoea, fever and vomiting.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: These symptoms are similar to other forms of food-borne infections or gastroenteritis.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: That is to say, the prescribed infectious diseases are subsets of the infectious diseases listed in the First Schedule.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: Support for persons whose livelihood is seriously affected by public health measures is important.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: Additional help was also provided through the Community Development Council.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: These are some examples of viable sources of assistance, and my Ministry will work with the relevant agencies to ensure that adequate support is provided where necessary.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: To Mr Murali Pillai and Dr Chia Shi-Lu's comment on whether there are appeal mechanisms for persons placed on stop-work orders or movement restrictions, I wish to clarify that placing persons on such orders is meant to prevent disease spread.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: As necessary, my Ministry will review requests for such persons to conduct specific activities, so long as public health and safety are not compromised.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: It is, indeed, important for my Ministry to be able to activate the community quickly in times of crisis.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: We have a reserve pool of trained contact tracing officers from within the public healthcare family.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: This will further augment our ability to quickly ramp up our public health responses.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: I agree with Mr Louis Ng and Mr Melvin Yong that the powers conferred to my Ministry and its officers should be accompanied by checks and balances.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: In implementing public health measures, there is sometimes tension between individual liberties and the common good.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: In deciding the extent and duration of public health measures, we take into account relevant considerations, including disease characteristics, expert advice and recommended practices, and conduct thorough risk assessments.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: For example, the number of days a person is subjected to surveillance or quarantine is dependent on the disease’s incubation period.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: Likewise, the duration a person is restricted from certain types of occupation is related to the risk of disease transmission.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: The approval of the Director of Medical Services, guided by professional ethics and advised by risk assessments, would be sought for such decisions.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: In closing, I would like to reiterate that the proposed amendments are meant to enhance the ability to detect infectious diseases threats, prevent their entry into Singapore, respond to outbreaks and arrest further spread.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: There are legislative and operational safeguards to ensure that the powers under the Act are used appropriately and judiciously.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: For measures that are farther-reaching or more restrictive, my Ministry has ensured that a stronger governing authority is present.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: For example, the Director of Medical Services, the chief medical officer and lead of the medical profession, provides oversight for many of the measures under the Act.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: I am confident that the revised Act will help us to further build our capabilities towards the prevention and control of infectious diseases.
